2024 · Research

A research year on two coasts

In 2024 the materials work moved to Perth, Western Australia, the brick design took a large step with the hinge-lock concept, and a small Ocean Supercluster grant brought the research programme back to Vancouver for 2025.

By the end of 2023 the project had a material, a lease on a small manufacturing space on Venables Street in Vancouver, and more questions than people. 2024 was the year the research spread out.

Perth

Much of the materials work moved to Perth, where director Ory Lavallee and engineer Chris Fisher, with support from the Western Australian government, continued where the UBC team had left off. They developed a simpler and faster manufacturing process using a slightly different formulation. They also showed that a composite made with sargassum, the floating seaweed that washes up in enormous quantities on Caribbean and West African coasts, could reach the same strength as one made with kelp. For a material whose supply chain was its weakest link, that mattered.

The hinge-lock

At the same time the shape of the brick changed. Working with Brady Kirk and Xiaoyuan Geng on 3D design and printing, the team replaced the earlier tongue-and-bump locking system with a concept called the hinge-lock, which allowed bricks to be joined and separated with far less force while holding more securely. In September 2024 the hinge-lock was declared the final form for patent purposes and sent to counsel. (The design was very popular with children, which turned out to be a useful test.)

Waterproofing, and a return to Vancouver

Late in 2024 Canada's Ocean Supercluster awarded the project a $25,000 Ocean Startup grant to run a validation study of a new waterproofing method. The plan: a team of UBC Materials Engineering students, supervised by two of the project's engineering advisors, would test a mineral-based waterproofing strategy that needed no petrochemical inputs and could not shed microparticles into the sea. That study is the subject of the next article.

Elsewhere in 2024

The year also brought three new patent filings on kelp processing and farming, a pilot of advance "claims" on future bricks, grants from the Arbitrum Foundation and Elephant Room for the digital platform behind those claims, and a letter of intent with a coastal First Nation about a prototype floating building. Not all of those threads continued. The ones that did are on the story page.
